title: Habits and Verb Patterns
description: Membicarakan kebiasaan, gaya hidup, dan perubahan. Kamu akan belajar verb + -ing dan verb + to-infinitive, used to untuk kebiasaan di masa lalu, serta be used to / get used to untuk beradaptasi dengan hal baru.
objectives: Memilih pola verb + -ing atau verb + to-infinitive untuk kata kerja yang umum
Membicarakan kebiasaan dan keadaan di masa lalu dengan used to / didn't use to
Membedakan used to + V1 dari be used to / get used to + noun / V-ing
Menceritakan perubahan gaya hidup dengan kosakata seperti take up, give up dan cut down on

lessons.title: Verbs Followed by -ing
lessons.summary: Memakai V-ing setelah kata kerja seperti enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, suggest, keep, give up dan consider.
objectives: Mengenali kata kerja yang selalu diikuti V-ing
Memakai V-ing setelah preposition (good at, interested in, ...)
Membentuk kalimat positive, negative dan pertanyaan dengan pola verb + -ing
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Verb + verb
In English, when one verb follows another verb, the second verb has a special form. Kadang bentuknya **V-ing** (*enjoy swimming*), kadang **to + V1** (*decide to swim*). Tidak ada aturan logis yang sempurna — kita harus **menghafal** kata kerja yang umum. In this lesson we focus on verbs followed by **-ing**.

You already know some from A1: *I like / love / hate cooking.*

### Kata kerja + V-ing
| Verb | Arti | Contoh |
|---|---|---|
| enjoy | menikmati | I enjoy **reading** before bed. |
| avoid | menghindari | Try to avoid **eating** late at night. |
| finish | selesai | Have you finished **cleaning** your room? |
| (not) mind | (tidak) keberatan | I don't mind **waiting**. |
| suggest | menyarankan | Rina suggested **taking** a taxi. |
| keep | terus-menerus | He keeps **checking** his phone. |
| give up | berhenti (kebiasaan) | She gave up **eating** meat. |
| consider | mempertimbangkan | We're considering **moving** to Tanjung Arum. |
| can't stand | sangat tidak suka | I can't stand **waiting** in queues. |
| practise / miss / imagine | berlatih / rindu / membayangkan | I miss **living** near the sea. |

Useful polite request: ***Would you mind** opening the window?* = Bisakah kamu membuka jendela?

### Negative
To make the second verb negative, put **not** before the -ing form: *I suggest **not** going out in this storm.* Untuk kata kerja pertama, gunakan auxiliary biasa: *I **don't** enjoy cooking.*

### Setelah preposition → selalu V-ing
This is a very useful rule: after a preposition (*at, in, of, about, for, before, after, without*), the verb is always **-ing**.
- *She's good **at** drawing.*
- *I'm interested **in** learning Korean.*
- *Thanks **for** helping me.*
- *Wash your hands **before** eating.*

### Ejaan -ing (review)
- make → making (hapus -e)
- stop → stopping, swim → swimming (gandakan konsonan)
- lie → lying

### Hati-hati
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita tidak mengubah bentuk kata kerja: *Saya menikmati membaca*. Karena itu pelajar sering menulis ✗ *I enjoy to read* atau ✗ *I enjoy read*. Remember: **enjoy + -ing**, always.

lessons.title: Verbs Followed by To-Infinitive
lessons.summary: Memakai to + V1 setelah kata kerja seperti decide, hope, plan, agree, refuse, promise, manage, offer dan afford, dan membandingkannya dengan verb + -ing.
objectives: Mengenali kata kerja yang diikuti to + V1
Membuat bentuk negative dengan not to + V1
Memilih antara verb + -ing dan verb + to-infinitive
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Verb + to + V1
In A2 you learned *want to, need to, would like to*. Many other common verbs follow the same pattern: **verb + to + V1** (to-infinitive). Banyak di antaranya berhubungan dengan **keputusan, rencana, harapan, dan janji** — hal yang mengarah ke masa depan.

| Verb | Arti | Contoh |
|---|---|---|
| decide | memutuskan | We decided **to stay** at home. |
| hope | berharap | I hope **to see** you soon. |
| plan | berencana | They're planning **to open** a bakery. |
| agree | setuju | He agreed **to help** us. |
| refuse | menolak | She refused **to answer**. |
| promise | berjanji | I promise **to call** you tonight. |
| manage | berhasil (walaupun sulit) | Did you manage **to find** a seat? |
| offer | menawarkan (diri) | Tono offered **to carry** my bag. |
| afford | mampu (membeli) | I can't afford **to buy** a new laptop. |
| learn / seem / expect | belajar / tampaknya / mengharapkan | She seems **to be** tired. |

### Negative: not to + V1
Put **not** before *to*: *I decided **not to** go.* (Aku memutuskan untuk tidak pergi.) Bandingkan: *I **didn't decide** to go* = aku tidak memutuskan untuk pergi — artinya berbeda.

### -ing atau to + V1?
| + V-ing | + to + V1 |
|---|---|
| enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, keep | decide, hope, plan, agree, refuse |
| suggest, consider, give up, can't stand | promise, manage, offer, afford, learn |

A rough tip: verbs about **future plans and decisions** often take *to + V1*; verbs about **experiences and feelings** often take *-ing*. Ini hanya tips, bukan aturan pasti — tetap hafalkan daftarnya.

### Kata kerja yang bisa keduanya
Some verbs can take both forms with almost the same meaning: **like, love, hate, start, begin, continue**.
- *It started **raining** / **to rain**.*
- *I like **cooking** / **to cook**.*

A few verbs (*stop, remember, try, forget*) change meaning with -ing or to — kamu akan mempelajarinya di level B2.

### Hati-hati
- ✗ *I hope seeing you* → ✓ *I hope **to see** you.*
- ✗ *She refused answering* → ✓ *She refused **to answer**.*
- Setelah *to* selalu **V1**: ✗ *I decided to went* → ✓ *I decided to go*.

lessons.title: Used To: Past Habits and States
lessons.summary: Membicarakan kebiasaan dan keadaan di masa lalu yang sudah tidak terjadi lagi dengan used to, didn't use to dan Did you use to...?
objectives: Memakai used to + V1 untuk kebiasaan dan keadaan di masa lalu
Membuat negative dan pertanyaan dengan didn't use to / Did ... use to?
Membedakan used to dari past simple untuk kejadian satu kali
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Used to = dulu (sekarang tidak lagi)
We use **used to + V1** to talk about habits or states in the past that are **not true now**. Dalam bahasa Indonesia biasanya kita memakai kata **dulu** atau **dulu sering**.
- *I **used to** play football every Saturday.* (Dulu aku main bola setiap Sabtu — sekarang tidak.)
- *This café **used to** be a bookshop.* (Dulu kafe ini toko buku.)

Used to works for two things:
| Jenis | Contoh |
|---|---|
| **Past habits** (kebiasaan berulang) | We used to visit our grandparents every holiday. |
| **Past states** (keadaan) | He used to have long hair. / I used to live in Pinewood. |

### Bentuk
| | Bentuk | Contoh |
|---|---|---|
| Positive | used to + V1 | She **used to** work in a bank. |
| Negative | didn't use to + V1 | I **didn't use to** like coffee. |
| Question | Did + subject + use to + V1? | **Did** you **use to** walk to school? |

Perhatikan: dalam negative dan pertanyaan, *did* sudah menunjukkan past, jadi kita menulis **use to** (tanpa -d) — sama seperti *didn't play*, bukan *didn't played*. You can also say **never used to**: *I never used to eat breakfast.*

### Used to vs past simple
Used to is only for **repeated** habits or long states. Untuk kejadian **satu kali** atau jumlah kali yang spesifik, pakai **past simple**:
- ✓ *I went to Lombok three times last year.*
- ✗ *I used to go to Lombok three times last year.*
- ✓ *I used to go to Lombok every summer when I was a child.*

Past simple juga bisa dipakai untuk kebiasaan (*I walked to school every day*), tetapi **used to** lebih jelas menunjukkan bahwa kebiasaan itu **sudah berubah**.

### Tidak ada bentuk present
There is no present form *use to*. Untuk kebiasaan sekarang, pakai present simple + **usually**:
- ✗ *I use to get up at six.*
- ✓ *I **usually** get up at six.*

### Pengucapan
*Used to* dan *use to* diucapkan sama: /ˈjuːs tə/. Jadi saat menulis, ingat aturan *did* di atas.

lessons.title: Be Used To and Get Used To
lessons.summary: Mengenal be used to (sudah terbiasa) dan get used to (mulai terbiasa) + noun / V-ing, dan membedakannya dari used to + V1.
objectives: Memakai be used to + noun/V-ing untuk sesuatu yang sudah biasa
Memakai get used to + noun/V-ing untuk proses menjadi terbiasa
Membedakan used to + V1, be used to + V-ing dan get used to + V-ing
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Tiga bentuk yang mirip
These three forms look similar but have different meanings. Ini sering membingungkan, jadi perhatikan tabel berikut.

| Bentuk | Arti | Contoh |
|---|---|---|
| **used to + V1** | dulu (sekarang tidak) | I **used to live** alone. |
| **be used to + noun / V-ing** | sudah terbiasa | I**'m used to living** alone. |
| **get used to + noun / V-ing** | mulai/menjadi terbiasa | I'm **getting used to living** alone. |

### Be used to = sudah terbiasa
**Be used to** means something is **normal and familiar** for you; it isn't strange or difficult any more. Kata *to* di sini adalah **preposition**, jadi diikuti **noun** atau **V-ing** (ingat lesson 1: setelah preposition selalu V-ing).
- *I'm used to **the noise** of the city.* (noun)
- *She's used to **getting up** early.* (V-ing)
- *He **isn't used to** cold weather.* (belum terbiasa)
- *Are you used to **working** at night?*

Bagian **be** berubah sesuai waktu: *I **was** used to it*, *I **wasn't** used to it at first*.

### Get used to = menjadi terbiasa (proses)
**Get used to** describes the **process** of something becoming normal. Kita sering memakainya dengan berbagai tense:
- *I'm **getting used to** my new job.* (sedang dalam proses)
- *It took me a month to **get used to** driving on the left.*
- *Don't worry — you'**ll get used to** it!*
- *She **got used to** the spicy food very quickly.*

### Contoh cerita singkat
*When Tari moved to Northfield, she **wasn't used to** the cold. At first it was hard, but slowly she **got used to** it. Now she **is used to** wearing a thick coat every day. She **used to** wear sandals all year in Indonesia!*

### Hati-hati
- ✗ *I'm used to get up early.* → ✓ *I'm used to **getting** up early.*
- ✗ *I used to getting up early.* (tanpa *be* → artinya 'dulu', jadi harus V1)
- Jangan lupa **be**: ✗ *I used to the noise now.* → ✓ *I**'m** used to the noise now.*

Tip: tanyakan pada dirimu — apakah ada **be/get** sebelum *used to*? Kalau ya → noun/V-ing. Kalau tidak → V1.

lessons.title: Changing Your Lifestyle
lessons.summary: Menceritakan perubahan gaya hidup dengan phrasal verbs seperti take up, give up, cut down on dan stick to, sambil menggabungkan used to dan verb patterns.
objectives: Memakai kosakata dan phrasal verbs tentang kebiasaan dan gaya hidup
Menggabungkan used to, be/get used to dan verb patterns untuk menceritakan perubahan
Membandingkan kehidupan dulu dan sekarang dengan jelas
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Membicarakan perubahan gaya hidup
People often change their habits: they start exercising, stop eating junk food, or move to a new place. To describe these changes, we combine everything from this unit: **used to**, **be/get used to**, and **verb patterns**.

### Phrasal verbs penting
| Phrasal verb | Arti | Pola | Contoh |
|---|---|---|---|
| take up | mulai (hobi/kegiatan baru) | + noun / V-ing | I've taken up yoga. |
| give up | berhenti (kebiasaan) | + noun / V-ing | He gave up smoking. |
| cut down on | mengurangi | + noun / V-ing | I'm cutting down on sugar. |
| stick to | tetap pada (rencana) | + noun | It's hard to stick to a diet. |
| stay up | begadang | (late) | I used to stay up until 2 a.m. |

Note that *give up* and *take up* are followed by **-ing** when the next word is a verb: *take up running, give up eating meat.*

### Struktur cerita 'dulu vs sekarang'
A clear description of change usually has three parts:
1. **The past**: *I used to eat a lot of fried food and I didn't use to exercise.*
2. **The change**: *Last year I decided to change. I gave up fizzy drinks and took up cycling.*
3. **Now**: *At first it was hard, but now I'm used to cycling to work. I enjoy feeling healthier.*

Perhatikan bagaimana setiap bagian memakai grammar dari unit ini: **used to** (dulu), **decide to / give up + -ing** (perubahan), **be used to / enjoy + -ing** (sekarang). Kamu juga bisa memakai **present perfect** dari Unit 1: *I've lost five kilos since I started.*

### Kosakata gaya hidup
- **lifestyle** — gaya hidup; **a healthy / an unhealthy lifestyle**
- **balanced diet** — pola makan seimbang
- **commute** — perjalanan pulang-pergi kerja (*My commute takes an hour.*)
- **work-life balance** — keseimbangan kerja dan kehidupan pribadi
- **routine** — rutinitas

### Tips
Gunakan kata penghubung waktu agar ceritamu runtut: *when I was younger, a few years ago, at first, after a while, nowadays*. Dan ingat: kebiasaan sekarang memakai **present simple** + *usually*, bukan *use to*.

sections.summary: To describe lifestyle changes, use **used to** for the past, **decide to / give up / take up / cut down on** for the change, and **be used to / enjoy + -ing** or present simple for now. questions.prompt: Talk for about one minute about how your lifestyle has changed in the last few years. Say what you used to do, what changed, and what you are used to now. Use at least two verb patterns (e.g. decided to, gave up + -ing, enjoy + -ing).
questions.sampleAnswer: A few years ago I used to stay up very late and I didn't use to do any exercise. I also used to spend two hours commuting every day. Last year I decided to change my routine. I gave up drinking fizzy drinks and I took up cycling. At first it was difficult, but now I'm used to getting up early, and I really enjoy riding my bike to work.
questions.explanation: Strukturkan jawabanmu: dulu (*used to / didn't use to*), perubahan (*decided to, gave up, took up*), sekarang (*I'm used to + V-ing, I enjoy + V-ing*).
